headline: Workday has agreed to buy C1.ai, a start-up whose software controls which employees and AI agents can reach a company's systems.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a confirmed acquisition by a large business-software company, but a small deal in a narrow field with no price given.
importance_line: Workers who wait for access to company systems and security teams that must track what AI agents can reach are the intended beneficiaries, but the benefits described are Workday's own claims, no price is given, and the deal has not yet closed.
summary: Workday, the US maker of HR, finance and IT software, announced at its Rising conference in Las Vegas on 13 October 2026 that it has signed a definitive agreement to buy C1.ai, a start-up whose software connects to a company's email, finance, code and cloud systems and gives each person and each AI agent the right access, removing it when it is no longer needed. The release gives no price and says the deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of Workday's fiscal 2027, which ends on 31 January 2027, subject to customary conditions; it cites C1.ai research that 95 percent of large US companies already run autonomous agents and Deloitte research that only 21 percent have a mature way to govern them.
notes: The Business Journals page (pool link) blocked with HTTP 403; read Workday's own press release on PR Newswire. The release does not say where C1.ai is based; The Business Journals headline says Portland.
